metadata.note: Skill teardown of skills/make/fashionista/SKILL.md (SOURCE-SNAPSHOT SHA-256 22614f44…; supervisor's episode.source_sha256 1b129e85…). The reel explains that `fashionista` is an EXPERIMENT in AI describability — not a fashion series. It teaches the three-beat structure (INTRO / VIDEO / OUTRO), the GATE ASK rule (never name the garment), VIDEO IS THE MASTER CLOCK (inverts audio-first law), STATED CONFIDENCE, the two error sources (generator vs describer), and the CALLS.json ledger that closes the correction loop. No fashion demo is run — this teardown is source-backed per SELF-DEMO LAW's feasibility fallback. Uses ClaudeTitleOutro (OUTRO-LOCK.md locked @NikBearBrown handle); @HumanitariansAI is the playlist folder chip inside composer beats. Kokoro am_onyx throughout — free, local. No captions.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST — anatomy of the fashionista skill folder plus the artifacts a trial produces.
beats.narration_text: First, the anatomy. A skill in this toolkit is a folder Claude reads before working. The fashionista folder is short by design. SKILL.md is the doctrine — three beats, eight gates, one register. The gates enforce the experiment: full-frame video, no on-screen text, subject-only narration, an ask that never names the garment. And the artifact each day writes is the same shape every time — a CALLS.json ledger, one row per garment term claimed, with a verdict slot waiting for a human to fill in.

beats.role_note: The pipeline — the three-beat structure INTRO / VIDEO / OUTRO. Input: a source clip. Output: one trial + a CALLS row.
beats.narration_text: The structure of one episode is short and rigid. INTRO, two to three seconds — the Claude composer asks what someone is wearing, never naming the garment. THE VIDEO, full frame — the source clip plays and Liam's commentary rides on top. OUTRO, two to three seconds — the title card holds while a spoken correction ask goes out to the audience. Total runtime equals clip duration plus about five seconds. Video is the master clock — the reel does not stretch, does not pad, does not slow.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — GATE ASK. The cold-open ask never contains the garment name. This is the sharpest, most enforceable rule in the skill.
beats.narration_text: First design decision, and it is the sharpest. GATE ASK — the cold-open ask never contains the garment name. The default is `Hey Claude, what is she wearing?` or `Hey Claude, what is he wearing?` — that pattern, nothing more. If the ask text contains any garment term from the beat sheet, the build fails. The naming is the AI's job, on camera. That rule guarantees the video is a real test — the answer cannot leak into the question.

beats.role_note: Design decision 2 — VIDEO IS THE MASTER CLOCK. Inverts the parent explainer's audio-first law.
beats.narration_text: Second design decision. Every other skill in this toolkit is audio-first — the narration is generated, then the visuals conform to it. Fashionista inverts that law and says so in every build log. The video is the master clock. Extract frames first, build a motion timeline — what happens at what second. Write the call against that timeline. And if the narration runs long — do not stretch the clip, do not loop it, do not freeze-pad it, do not slow it. Cut words. The video does not move.

props.heading: Video is the master clock.
props.body: Extract frames → build a MOTION TIMELINE (what happens at what second) → write the call against that timeline. Never stretch · never loop · never freeze-pad · never slow. If the call runs long, CUT WORDS — the video does not move.

beats.role_note: Design decision 3 — STATED CONFIDENCE. Sports-announcer register. Hedging is content.
beats.narration_text: Third decision. The register is sports announcer with stated confidence. Present tense. Short sentences. Energy. And every garment term is spoken with a confidence the viewer can hear. `That's a sherwani — I'm confident.` Or: `I want to say lehenga, but the length is fighting me on that.` Hedging is not weakness. It is the content. And when the announcer catches themselves reaching for the famous word over the precise one — lehenga, kimono, kaftan, blazer — they name that failure mode out loud. That is the honest signal the audience is scoring.

beats.role_note: Falsifiability — two stacked error sources. GENERATOR ERROR vs DESCRIBER ERROR. The move nobody else in AI-video makes.
beats.narration_text: Falsifiability, and this is where the skill earns its keep. These are generated garments. So a wrong episode can be wrong in two distinct ways. Generator error — the render shows something no real garment of that type does. The image is wrong. Describer error — the render is coherent and the name is wrong. The call is wrong. When they are separable, the announcer says which one. When they are not, they say that too. Nobody else in AI video separates those two lanes, and that is the most interesting thing this series does.

beats.role_note: Design tell — the CALLS.json ledger. The verdict slot stays null until a human fills it. Without this the loop evaporates.
beats.narration_text: Design tell. Each day writes a small file — books slash fashionista slash date slash CALLS.json — one row per garment term claimed. Term, confidence, reasoning, timestamp in the clip, alternatives considered, and a verdict slot that stays null until a human fills it from the comments. That is why the outro's spoken ask is mandatory. `If you know this garment, tell me what I got wrong.` Every episode. Without that ask, the verdict slot never fills, and the correction loop evaporates. The ledger is the artifact the whole skill exists to produce.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates the skill.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. Fashionista is an experiment, not a fashion series. Every episode is one trial. The audience is the scoring function, and the uncertainty is the subject. Gate ask keeps the answer out of the question. Video is the master clock. Every garment term is spoken with stated confidence — hedging is content. And two stacked error sources — generator versus describer — get logged in a CALLS.json ledger with a verdict slot waiting for you. Skip the correction ask and the loop evaporates. Do it well and the series has something to falsify.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer with a paste-ready prompt Liam reads aloud + discusses. Dry-run planning pass — no source video needed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code: read the fashionista skill, then plan a dry-run trial. Pick a garment you have seen in a photo, draft an ask that never names it, and write a candidate CALLS.json row — term, confidence, reasoning, two alternatives considered, and verdict null. Then answer one more question. If your call turned out to be wrong, would it be a generator error or a describer error? Or is it not separable? Read Claude's plan and check three things. Does the drafted ask stay inside the `what is he wearing` pattern? Does the row have all six fields including the null verdict? And does Claude commit to which error lane matters most, or say honestly that it cannot tell?

props.command: Read skills/make/fashionista/SKILL.md. Do not run any paid API.
